videos.text:
What does Vitamin D actually do?

A LOT more than most people realize…

That’s because vitamin D isn’t just a vitamin, it a hormone your body produces when sunlight hits your skin

But even if you live in a sunny climate, chances are… you're still not getting enough

50–70% of the global population is either deficient or insufficient

I live in San Diego, one of the sunniest cities on Earth, and my blood test last year still came back clinically deficient at 18 ng/mL 🙃

And it matters because low vitamin D doesn’t just affect your bones or your immune system

→ It impacts your mood
→ Your hormones
→ Your energy
→ Your sleep
→ Literally how your body functions

And from personal experience, supplementing consistently for 3 months made a bigger difference in how I felt than almost anything else I’ve done for my health

One last thing though:

If you do supplement, make sure you're also getting vitamin K (specifically K2)
 Vitamin D increases calcium absorption, but K2 helps guide it where it belongs (like bones and teeth) instead of places it doesn’t (like arteries)

So the two work best as a team

For Dosing, between 5,000-10,000IU daily is best for correcting a deficiency, and between 2,000-5,000IU daily is considered a healthy maintenance dose.

I take Legion’s (in my bio), but Thorne, NOW Foods, and Bulksupplements have good D+K supplements as well
